summary: Tenant edge header rewrite causes pin to be claimed during canary prewarm, producing mixed model responses
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary prewarm for model redwood/llama-3b-v1, several tenants observed mixed responses where requests that should have stayed on the pinned variant returned outputs from the canary variant. Impact: Customer reported regression in inference outputs (semantic differences) and elevated token consumption for pinned sessions. This affects a dedicated customer in prod (Acme Health) and is causing customer-facing errors for health-reporting microservices that rely on deterministic outputs. Environment: production (us-east-1) dedicated capacity pool for Acme Health. Canary rollout initiated 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC; prewarm traffic started 02:05 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer pins route to redwood/llama-3b-v1 via dashboard or route header. 2) Initiate staged canary promotion to redwood/llama-3b-quantized-v1 with prewarm mirror enabled. 3) Simulate tenant traffic with X-Tenant-ID and X-Prefer-Model headers set; note that customer has a CDN that rewrites headers (X-Tenant-ID -> X-Tenant). 4) Observe that sessions previously pinned to v1 begin receiving canary responses intermittently. Logs / traces: - Edge ingress logs show header mutation: "X-Tenant-ID: 84231" rewritten to "X-Tenant: 84231" for ~15% of requests during prewarm window. - Orchestrator audit shows "claim_session" events for tenant 84231 at 02:06:12 from prewarm worker (prewarm-worker-7). - Routing mesh traces show a pin-update event followed by immediate request routing to the canary variant. - Observability dashboard: token rate spike for tenant 84231 between 02:05-02:10 UTC; request latency stable. Initial hypothesis: The prewarm worker performs an opportunistic claim operation to populate KV cache and prewarm model shards. Because the edge header rewrite changed the tenant header name, the orchestrator treated mutated requests as a different session identifier and the claim logic exercised a higher-precedence path that overwrote the existing pin for tenant sessions (claim precedence > explicit pin). Race condition between prewarm claim and pinned-session lease refresh resulted in transient ownership change and mixed responses.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:15 - Maya Patel (Support): Received report from Acme Health via support channel. Customer provides sample request IDs and example outputs showing semantic drift. Asked for diagnostic permission and requested attach of ingress logs.

2026-03-12 10:02 - SRE triage (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced condition in staging using tenant header rewrite. Observed prewarm worker performing claim_session and TTL on claim appears to be non-isolated from explicit pin. Created INT-4451 for deeper orchestrator audit and race analysis.
2026-03-12 12:20 - Customer (Acme Health): Applied temporary header pass-through rule at CDN edge (preventing X-Tenant-ID rename). Reported decreased occurrence of mixed responses after change.

2026-03-13 08:30 - Engineering (Priya Rao): Confirmed prewarm-worker implements force-claim to accelerate KV population. Policy evaluation currently treats force-claim as able to supersede pinned leases when session keys differ (header mutation case). Proposed short-term mitigation: change prewarm claim path to include 'do-not-override-pins' flag when operating on dedicated customer pools.

2026-03-13 11:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Communicated workaround to Acme Health: add CDN rule to avoid header renaming OR explicitly include X-Model-Pin header to reaffirm pinned variant while we deploy a mitigation. Customer accepted workaround and requested timeline for engineering fix.

2026-03-13 17:40 - Engineering (Liam O'Connor): Patch PR opened to add flag and to make prewarm claims lower precedence than explicit session pins. Referential PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4567. Targeted rollback window: next midnight deploy window (2026-03-14 00:00 UTC).
investigation_notes: Findings: 1) The effective session key used by the orchestrator is derived from a canonical header set. Edge mutators can inadvertently split identity (X-Tenant vs X-Tenant-ID). 2) Prewarm claims are executed by workers with elevated permissions and were not respecting explicit pin leases in dedicated pools. 3) The race surface exists when a prewarm claim and a tenant's lease refresh occur within the same 1-2 second window; race can temporarily flip routing until lease reconciliation completes. Evidence: orchestrator audit logs and prewarm-worker traces correlated via request IDs. Priority: High due to deterministic customer impact and potential to repeat on other tenants with edge header rewrites.
resolution: Mitigation (short-term): - Instructed Acme Health to disable header rewrite at their CDN (confirmed reduction in incidents). - Applied temporary ACL in routing mesh to block requests missing canonical tenant header. Mitigation (engineering, medium-term): - PR #4567 introduced 'do-not-override-pins' flag for prewarm claims and changes claim precedence so explicit pins are authoritative; scheduled for deploy 2026-03-14 00:00 UTC. Follow-ups: - Add telemetry alert for prewarm-claim events that attempt to override pins. - Update runbook to include header-canonicalization checks before canary prewarm is enabled. Current status: Waiting on deploy verification. No customer-facing code rollback required. Postmortem: Pending (will link when available).
